parts.note: a musician who bows a violin while perched on a roof in a famous stage musical, hence a show

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flamboyant arbour built on top of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bower' looks like a garden arbour but is one who bows a violin; 'Showy' points to the musical Fiddler on the Roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist draws a bow across the strings, and the musical's title character plays on a roof.

parts.note: agents who act for others, and things that work together towards a result, like elements travelling alongside one another

explanation.surface: Spies working for communist sympathisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow-travellers' suggests political sympathisers; a factor is a commercial agent and also one of several contributing elements.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a business agent, and contributing elements combine to produce an outcome.

clue.text: Ernest lies abed in order to show such calmness

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order to display the answer

explanation.surface: A man named Ernest stays in bed to prove how relaxed he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried, careful composure in action.

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, the letters held within it

explanation.surface: A dazzling light from a particular dye.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl or frowning look; to lour is to look sullen.

indicators.note: stewing turns the letters to mush, rearranging them

parts.note: the word with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: An English person's cooked apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' rearranges BRITONS; here the 's gives a letter. Ribston Pippin is an English apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ribston Pippin is an old English dessert variety of the fruit.

parts.note: a hospital room where patients are put to get better

explanation.surface: The familiar phrase saying something could be done better.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'room for improvement' is read literally: a room where the sick improve.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital chamber holds patients while they recover their health.

parts.note: people who stand and wait, and those who serve at table

explanation.surface: A remark about staff who stand while serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant staff serve diners, and those who wait stand by.

definitions.meaning: to travel on a bus or bicycle

explanation.surface: An instruction to rise and move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Get up on a horse and go; and to be carried as a passenger.

clue.text: For a scientist, fake diamonds take half an hour

parts.note: paste is glass used for imitation gems

indicators.note: half of the word, its second half

explanation.surface: A scientist's fake gems take thirty minutes to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half an' takes the back half of 'hour'. Louis Pasteur was the French chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French microbiologist behind pasteurisation.

parts.note: beauty is only skin deep, and these doctors treat skin

explanation.surface: Cosmetic doctors who care about looks and nothing beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'beauty is only skin deep' is turned around: skin specialists claim beauty goes no deeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians specialising in skin diseases.

clue.text: Condition causing one to stop driving at green?

definitions.text: Condition causing one to stop driving at green?

parts.words: Condition causing one to stop driving at green?
parts.note: a sight defect that confuses red and green traffic lights, so a driver might halt at the wrong one

explanation.surface: A motorist's puzzling habit of braking when the lights say go.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to tell red from green might halt at a go signal.

parts.note: 'or' introduces an alternative
BS is the abbreviation for British Standard, a UK quality mark

explanation.surface: A choice between a quality mark and spheres.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres or balls, such as the royal regalia orb.

definitions.meaning: to put counterfeit money into circulation
complete, absolute, as in total nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone spends money until the whole sum is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing forged coin is the legal sense of the verb; as an adjective it means complete or absolute.

definitions.meaning: an old dialect name for a duck such as the wigeon
the ungrammatical 'it's me', slurred to 's me, instead of 'tis I

explanation.surface: Someone calls out to a loved one, admitting their phrasing is clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is also a British term of endearment, which the surface uses; the second definition is the sloppy form 's me said quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect bird name for a wild duck; and the casual spoken 's me sounds identical.

clue.text: The one-roomed cottage or the two with yard

parts.note: 'both' means the two together

explanation.surface: Choosing between a small cottage and two with a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a Scottish hut or farm-worker's cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a small hut or basic cottage.

explanation.surface: A question about a germ-ridden coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Infested with germs; and a light horse-drawn carriage.

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight or baronet, a noble
a loin is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A nobleman reduced in rank needs a second title.
explanation.walkthrough: A baron of beef is a joint made of two of these cuts left joined at the backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron of beef consists of a double joint of the prime upper-loin cut.

indicators.note: 'out' suggests the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician has been voted out of a constitutional seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks political but is the noun for a health walk; 'out' rearranges SEAT and RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a leisurely stroll taken for one's health.

definitions.meaning: things struck to make a flame

explanation.surface: A question about which games the attacking footballers will play.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighters struck on a box, and scheduled games between teams.

parts.note: Ma's, mother's
a pet is a fit of sulking, a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Mother's pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal but is a sulk; TIFF is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, powerful breed of guard dog.

explanation.surface: A hastily done scribble.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembled on the spot from whatever is at hand; and to make rough marks.

clue.text: Star revolver pointing the wrong way at us

indicators.note: the gun is pointed backwards, so its name is read from end to start

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol, loosely called a revolver
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film star's gun is aimed back at the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointing the wrong way' reverses LUGER to REGUL, before US.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest point in the constellation Leo is a named star.

clue.text: For example, at no time return for retaliation

indicators.note: a return is a turning back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
never means at no time

explanation.surface: Someone vows never to come back to take vengeance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses EG and NEVER together, giving REVEN + GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting one's own back, paying an injury in kind.

clue.text: Someday, perhaps, one will win at Cruft's

indicators.note: 'perhaps' implies the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A dog breeder hopes one day to win the top prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruft's is Britain's famous dog show; a Samoyed is a white Siberian dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of Siberian spitz that competes at the famous British dog show.

definitions.meaning: sang, past participle form, as notes produced by the voice
the ... dynasty, a period of Chinese civilisation

explanation.surface: A student jotted down observations on Chinese culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made notes' means produced musical notes with the voice, not wrote memos.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocal music produced, past participle; and the dynasty ruling China from 960 to 1279.

clue.text: Not the chief sort in Huxley's new world

definitions.text: Not the chief sort in Huxley's new world

parts.words: Not the chief sort in Huxley's new world
parts.note: a Native American warrior, below a chief, and the adjective in the title of Aldous Huxley's novel

explanation.surface: A remark about who is not in charge in a dystopian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal warrior who is not a leader; the word opens the title Brave New World.

clue.text: Old Celtic character found in fog among mountains

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the words that follow, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: An ancient Celt is found lost among misty mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham (also spelt this way) was the alphabet of early Irish inscriptions.

definitions.meaning: a dissolute man, from Hogarth's series The ... Progress
a toothed tool for gathering leaves

explanation.surface: An advanced kind of garden implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth's profligate makes a 'progress'; and a toothed implement for leaves.

clue.text: The deck is going up and down!

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up and coming down the grid

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A ship's deck heaving in a rough sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry reads the same in both directions, so it goes up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised deck at a ship's stern.

clue.text: All at once, throwing insults at anyone

indicators.note: throwing the words about mixes up their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hurls abuse at everyone in a single outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening in a single moment, immediately.

parts.note: the first family on earth, Adam and Eve's, had a third son in Genesis

explanation.surface: A question about who plays third for a club's top side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First team' looks like sport but means humanity's first family; the third son of Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, he was born to Adam and Eve after Cain and Abel.

clue.text: Formerly modelled for Etty and how!

definitions.text: Formerly modelled for Etty and how!

parts.note: ex- means former
posed as an artist's model

explanation.surface: A former model recalls sitting for the painter Etty, in a revealing way.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a Victorian painter famous for nudes, so someone who had modelled for him was laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Etty painted nudes, so a sitter was uncovered and on view.
